entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Bank of Russia (Central Bank of the Russian Federation) is Russia's central bank and supreme monetary authority, established in 1860 as the State Bank of the Russian Empire and reorganized in 1990 as an independent institution following the Soviet Union's collapse. As the world's seventh-largest holder of foreign currency reserves (approximately $600 billion before 2022 sanctions), the Bank of Russia used reserve accumulation as a geopolitical strategy under Governor Elvira Nabiullina.

Nabiullina, appointed by Putin in 2013 and reappointed in 2022, is considered one of the world's most capable central bankers: she managed Russia's 2014-2015 currency crisis (ruble fell 50% after Crimea annexation sanctions) through aggressive interest rate increases to 17%, and guided Russia through oil price shocks in 2020. Her 2022 reappointment amid the Ukraine war despite Western sanctions on Russia's central bank reserves was controversial.

The February 2022 Western freeze of approximately $300 billion of Russia's $600 billion foreign currency reserves — held in Western central banks and international institutions as part of sanctions following Russia's Ukraine invasion — was the most significant central bank asset seizure in history. The freeze demonstrated that foreign currency reserves held in Western institutions could be weaponized as a geopolitical tool, prompting China, India, and other nations to reconsider their reserve allocation strategies.
